learning_outcomes.text: Be able to solve problems related to electrical machines and installations.
Be able to write a technical report on work in the field of electrical machines and installations that includes a calculation part and an experimental part.
Be able to design a low-voltage electrical installation.
Be able to design a transformation center.
Be able to calculate and select the appropriate electrical drive for a machine or industrial process.
Know the current regulations related to electrical machines and installations.

syllabus_topics: TEMA 1 – GENERAL PRINCIPLES OF ROTATING ELECTRICAL MACHINES
First overview of classic rotating machines
Torque-speed characteristic of mechanical loads. Operating point and stability
Degrees of protection. Construction and mounting forms
Types of mechanical transmission and reducers
Structure and components of the electrical system
Elements that make up electrical installations in medium and low voltage
TEMA 6 – NEUTRAL REGIMES AND PEOPLE PROTECTION
Protection against direct and indirect contacts
Insulated cables in LV. Insulating and conductive materials
Sizing of protective pipes and ducts
TEMA 8 – PROTECTION OF LOW VOLTAGE ELECTRICAL INSTALLATIONS
Nature and cause of faults in electrical installations
Automatic circuit breaker and magnetothermal circuit breaker
Types of short circuits in electrical installations
Basic components and structure of a transformation center
Types of cells and medium voltage equipment
Asynchronous motor: operation under load, starting and speed regulation
Analysis and verification of a low voltage electrical installation and assembly of an electrical panel
Design and calculation of a low voltage electrical installation by computer

assessment_methods.method: Continuous Assessment: Laboratory practical work completion and submission
Continuous Assessment: Written theoretical-practical tests during the course

assessment_rules: The student passes the course if they obtain at least 5 out of 10 points in the global average grade. A minimum grade of 4.5 out of 10 is required for the final exam; if not met, the global average cannot exceed 4.5. Continuous assessment grades are only valid for the two calls of the current academic year. For the second call, the final exam accounts for 90% (70% original exam + 20% recovery of partial exams). In the extraordinary call for graduation, the final exam constitutes 100% of the grade with no minimum mark required. In case of fraud in the final exam, the grade will be 0 points for that call.
